method: Two local synthetic 8 MiB HTTP responses through the actual Unix-socket broker and separate fresh durable ledgers; broker deadline 8 seconds per request; outer timeout 20 seconds.
comparison: See throughput-probe.json. Before batching, durable-ledger runs were incomplete after 8 seconds and delivered approximately 0.84 and 0.76 MiB/s including headers. The pre-change measurements overlapped the active primary case; these post-change measurements did not. Ratios are therefore confounded by differences in host load.
limitations: Before and after ran under different host conditions; pre-change baseline overlapped the primary and may have contended for resources.
Loopback HTTP is not TLS, public network, remote source, candidate runtime, or scientific evidence of software performance.
Two samples per mode; no controlled host load or randomized crossover.
Prepaid reservations can overcount transmitted bytes; unused credit is not refunded, including on crash.
After samples may not reach disk saturation or reproduce real traffic chunking.
